reviews.title: Central is The Best Restaurant in The World. Read My Review and Understand Why
reviews.text:
Central is the best restaurant in the world that I have dined at. Not trying to sound conceited, but I have dined at the finest Michelin Star and Top 100 restaurants all over the globe. The U.S., Mexico, Homg Kong, Taiwan, Tokyo, Rome, Istanbul, Athens, and dozens of other cities in those countries plus others in the Middle East, Asia, Europe. Central is the best. It’s that good. 

The tasting menu we had offered 30-plus items and I ate every one, and absolutely enjoyed all completely but two, just on my taste.  That’s saying something. Of the total I’d say that 28 were positivity exquisite with some being beyond description - they were that good. At one point trying to describe the complexity of flavors (that I promise you never had before) my wife said “I don’t know whether to cry or scream.”  It’s that good. 

That was the food part. It doesn’t end there. The experience and presentation are without comparison. Like…if Central’s experience aspect is a 100 the second best 3-Star Michelin experience I had is a 70.  Here, with every dish they bring you out a tray of the actual ingredients and describe them. The meal is also replete with you being presented with books, cards and other references - to keep - that illustrate what you are eating. Lastly, every dish is served with different size utensils of different materials presented in different vessels, and unique, elegant and mindful plating. It’s positively exquisite. 

The restaurant itself is beautiful. Music plays in the background but it’s calming non-intrusive and is more like natural sound strung into music to enhance not interfere with the experience. Tables are stone and wood and large and welcoming and positioned so that so feel you are almost alone in the restaurant, and there are not many. On display always is the kitchen where you’ll observe all functions of the meals being prepared by a significant culinary staff, always disciplined, always seeming pleased to be sharing the evening with you. 

Then there is the service. Which again is beyond compare. Your servers (several)  and host will explain everything to you in fine detail and you’ll be surprised I promise by what you learn and the effort to find the most incredible ingredients and use them in such unique and special ways. My wife speaks Spanish. I, English. Every staff member took the time to explain everything to us in both languages. 

There are reviews here of less than 5 stars for Central and all I can say to that is that whoever posted them is not used to fine dining or doesn’t understand that the main experience of dining at this level is to awaken your taste buds to taste things you didn’t know existed, and love it. If that happens and the food tastes terrible that’s one thing. But if you eat here and don’t think the food tastes like other worldly love in small portions then that’s ok…but then respectfully fine dining at this level is just not for you. You have to appreciate dining at that level and that you’re experiencing something that is not just delicious but that most folks their whole life will never experience. You must be open to taste things that make you happy to be alive. 

I haven’t eaten at every restaurant in the world. But so far for me and my wife, Central is the best restaurant in the entire world.

reviews.title: A Memorable Experience for the Senses and the Mind
reviews.text:
Dining at Central was a refined experience rooted in precision and respect for Peruvian biodiversity. The meal unfolded with thoughtful restraint with each course elegant, deliberate, and deeply grounded. This was a cerebral, structured, balanced experience. 
Service was polished and professional, led by a youthful team that handled the room with care. Chef’s personal delivery of the first course was a subtle but powerful gesture. The overall energy of the space leaned masculine, in contrast to Kjolle’s warmth, but still held its own form of generosity. As someone in the industry, I felt seen, not in overt ways, but in the details that matter.

The only sour note was being questioned before entering the gate about whether I had a reservation. This didn’t happen the first time I entered that compound to dine at Kjolle. The contrast was noticeable. As an industry professional who naturally sees every detail, this particular moment showed a crack in the almost perfect hospitality.

Virgilio Martínez, the visionary chef and owner, is one of the most creative talents in the culinary world today. reviews.title: One of a kind Culinary Experience in Lima, Peru
reviews.text:
It has to be one of the top restaurant experiences in the world.  To say this place is outstanding is an understatement.  You start with an elegant entrance, and a decor that is inspirational.  Once at our table, our guide (it seems silly to call him, and the staff, waiters or servers) begins the explanation of what you are about to experience.
You are presented with a pre selected menu, with the various taste sensations one is about to explore.  We start with local ingredients at various altitudes, increasing altitude and delicacy along the way.  We explore the entire terrain of Peru with 13 different courses including fish and spices sourced from the Amazon.  Each course presented offers another culinary delight and surprise.  One wonders how their chefs are able to dream up such wonderful bites and that the next course seems to outdo the last.  They do present you with booklets explaining where the food comes from and other information about the journey.
We had a 1.30pm lunch reservation and didn’t finish until five pm.  We never felt rushed, or hurried through a course.  There was always ample time to savor whatever regional delicacy they placed before us.  I would highly recommend the local wine paring (local as in South American, although they do offer European wines), it was truly remarkable how well the wines went with our food.  My wife had the local non-alcoholic beverage pairing, also very good.
If you are planning on being in Lima, Peru, it is a must.  I must warn of two things.  
1.  Upon the recommendation of my travel agent, Isabel Calles at Latin Excursions, I made my reservation six months ahead of time when their reservation window opened for our travel dates.  It is very difficult to get in.
2.   One must think of this place as a one of a kind experience and an epicurean adventure, so consider it price wise as a French Laundry, or Per Se.
Having been to some of the most renown and exclusive restaurants in the US and Europe, I put this one in a class by itself.  Enjoy!

reviews.title: Gastronomic experience through Peru’s rich biodiversity. Deserved to be the best restaurant.
reviews.text:
Dining at Central Restaurante in Lima is an extraordinary culinary journey through Peru’s diverse ecosystems. The 13-course “Mundo en Desnivel” tasting menu offers a sensory expedition from the depths of the Pacific Ocean to the peaks of the Andes, with each dish representing a specific altitude and ecosystem. Chef Virgilio Martínez and his team masterfully craft each course using indigenous ingredients, presenting them with artistic flair that reflects Peru’s rich biodiversity. Each course was very interesting to us. 

The ambiance at Central is both elegant and immersive and you don’t feel ‘stiff ‘ and too formal. Located in the bohemian district of Barranco, the restaurant’s design integrates natural elements, creating a serene atmosphere that complements the dining experience. The open kitchen allows guests to observe the meticulous preparation of each dish, enhancing the connection between the food and its origins . ￼ ￼

Service is attentive and informative, with staff providing detailed explanations of each course’s ingredients and the ecosystems they represent. This educational aspect enriches the meal, offering insights into Peru’s geography and culinary heritage. The wine/ non- alcoholic pairing features selections that harmonize with the flavors of the dishes, further elevating the experience . The service was perfect orchestrated. They will refill your water or drinks when you finish with very attentive servers. They also explain the sequence how you enjoy each course with purposeful arranged dishes on your table. The transition within each course was seamless and you don’t want to wait long in between. My partner doesn’t eat seafood. They thoughtfully replaced it with a vegetarian ingredient rather than simply substitute with vegetarian dishes option.  Each staff seems to be given equal opportunity to ‘shine’ as they get to explain the dishes to us - good for staff development as not like certain staff just to be able to serve the dishes on the table but doesn’t explain the dishes. 

While the tasting menu is a significant amount of money, it is an indulgence gastronomic adventure. We felt full and satisfied with our meal as you can tell each component of the dish was thoughtfully curated and to the highest quality and standards. You can take away the books and menu which explains further of the Peru’ biodiversity. They became the number 1 restaurant in the world in 2023 and sometimes people might not be able to sustain the quality but I feel like Central still managed to maintain this and continue to evolve.

reviews.title: Our trip to Peru!
reviews.text:
Central in Lima was by far one of the most impressive dining experiences I have ever had. The concept of the restaurant is unique: Each passage represents a different altitude and region of Peru – from the Andes to the Amazon to the coast.

The presentation of the dishes is spectacular, almost like works of art, and at the same time they taste exceptionally good. Each bite tells a story about Peruvian biodiversity, culture and taste.

The service was first class: attentive, friendly and very professional. The staff explained each dish with passion and background knowledge.

The ambience is elegant, modern and warm at the same time – perfect for a special dinner.

Conclusion: If you are in Lima and interested in quality cuisine, Central should definitely not be missed. It’s more than just a dinner – it’s a sensory and cultural journey that will be remembered.

I had high expectations for Central, given its reputation, but unfortunately, it failed to deliver on multiple fronts.

First, the wine pairing was a major letdown. For the exorbitant price, I expected a well-thought-out selection that complemented the dishes, but instead, the choices felt uninspired and, at times, completely mismatched with the food. It seemed more like an afterthought than a carefully curated experience.

The service was another disappointment. While not outright rude, it was far from the level of attentiveness one would expect at a place charging these prices.

As for the food, while some dishes were enjoyable, nothing truly justified the sky-high prices. The overall experience left me feeling like I had paid for the prestige of the name rather than the quality of the meal itself.

If you’re looking for a place that genuinely delivers on fine dining, I’d recommend spending your money elsewhere. This was an overpriced, underwhelming experience that simply wasn’t worth it.

reviews.title: A culinary journey through Peru
reviews.text:
I'm no food critic, but given the opportunity to dine at Central, elected the world's second best restaurant, I dove in - because I love food, and I love to try different ingredients and concepts. Our dinner, to put it mildly, was epic. 

When our group of four was led in, we were given a tour of local ingredients, cutlery, ceramics, and everything else that would be relevant to our meal. Our table was a bit removed from the busiest part of the restaurant, which was perfect. It was Saturday and it was full.

The extensive tasting menu told an artistically narrated story. Called "Mundo em desnivel" (something akin to "sloped world"), it snaked between Peru's different altitudes and ecosystems, with carefully crafted dishes that took the diners on a sensorial journey through the country. Each dish was explained by staff and flawlessly presented. We were introduced to countless ingredients we had never heard of, in dishes that allowed us to taste every one of them. 

There were 14 in total. Even though the portions were small (as they have to be), by the end of this 3-hour meal we were more than satisfied, and absolutely enthralled. Is it expensive? Yes. Is life too short? Yes.

reviews.title: Beyond the Common
reviews.text:
Do you prefer traditional food than experimental cuisine? Are you afraid to experience unusual flavors due to the use of unconventional raw materials in the kitchen? If the answer is yes, maybe the 900€/couple is not well spent money, in your case.
The Central goes beyond these barriers, past the border of imaginary and conventional cuisine. Each dish is a work of art transformed into something that you eat, first with your eyes, then with your mouth. The delight is common to sight and taste. Some of the dishes are made with stuff that we didn't even know we could eat. This is the research work pre-work in the kitchen.
The menu turns a trip through Peru into an edible map, where each dish represents different regions, places and altitudes of that country. The presentation is sublime and the flavors open new horizons to the palate.
Apart table, the staff is friendly and competent, as would be expected. The space is exquisite and extremely welcoming, even with exhausted crowd. In our case, we loved the experience and that wonderful trip to the table.
The only thing I can identify is the price.
Being the raw material of Peruvian origin, as the restaurant proudly mentions, the exorbitant price makes even less sense.
Despite this point, the price, we like the experience, because that's what it is about: eating and traveling without leaving the table.  And that's extraordinary.

reviews.title: Overrated and a huge disappointment
reviews.text:
For what was meant to be the highlight of our trip to Peru, dining at Central (the #1 restaurant in the world) was a severe disappointment and highly overrated. Each course was texturally disappointing (everything is eaten with a spoon), oily, emulsified and just bland. The concept and restaurant itself is beautiful, aside from the fly buzzing around and spider on the table, but that doesn’t forgive the utterly dismal food and lack of flavor. If you like non descript seaweed, algae and black burnt ash powder on your food you will love this. We did have a pork dish that was essentially soft fat that tasted of propane gas and then bland beef cheek cream that was again emulsified and covered in foam and grey cream. Foam, so much oily foam on multiple plates. 

In a country where we have had an explosion of flavorful food, this was an incredibly sad example of the cuisine Peru is rightly proud of. I’d go as far to say it’s disrespectful to their cuisine and the people who work so hard to grow the produce and turn it into delicious food. Seriously there are SO many better options in Peru, do not be drawn into the trap of going to Central. 

I’m not a picky eater and will eat and try anything put in front of me, especially if it’s something new and local to a place I’m visiting, but this by far has been the worst dining experience I’ve had and sadly, was the one I’d most looked forward to.

reviews.title: Should have walked out and gotten pizza
reviews.text:
If you’re seeking a dining experience that leaves you questioning your life choices, look no further than this high flyer--in this writer's opinion, a five-star farce. For nearly $1100 for two persons, you’d expect a meal that tantalizes the senses, but what you get instead is an absurd parade of pretentious dishes that taste like they were conjured from the depths of a culinary nightmare. Each of the 13 "moments" was preceded by an unintelligible explanation of the sources of the ingredients.  For a dish featuring local seaweed, piles of untreated seaweed were displayed.  For a fish dish, four lacquered fish heads were likewise brought to the table.  Each plate is an exercise in silliness, as if the chef had a bet to create the most bizarre and flavorless combinations imaginable.  In short, not a single "moment" tasted good or was satisfying. 

The ambience? Imagine dining in a dark cavernous void, where a single spotlight glares down on your table like a bad stage performance, leaving you feeling both exposed and absurdly uncomfortable. It’s less “intimate dining” and more “you’re on trial.”  Nor is there any laughter or good cheer--only seriousness and the expectation of applauding the brilliance of the chef.  

A bottle of NZ sauvignon blanc which might cost $25 in your wine shop is marked up fourfold, and adds to the  small fortune one spends for the "experience,  but offers little relief from the disappointment that permeates the evening. 

Save your money and your palate—this restaurant is a shining example of how a high price tag can’t mask a total lack of substance. A true culinary tragedy.

reviews.title: Avoid this overpriced, mediocre restaurant
reviews.text: Way overpriced for the quality and experience. Big disappointment! No way this is a top world restaurant. One course is little tasteless potatoes. Will never return to this place.

reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.text: Came with my wife while we were on a family trip to Peru. Great atmosphere, the introduction to the ingredients was informative and the food was delicious (duh). The restaurant is pricey but if you compare it to other restaurants of the same caliber in other countries, Central is affordable (nuance and context matter). I would come back if I ever visit Lima again.

reviews.title: The most stunning, beautiful and weirdest flavor journey you might ever have.
reviews.text:
Amazing journey, full of surprising, punchy flavors.

The ambiance was perfect, big open kitchen, incredibly friendly service and decoration of the room is stunning. 

Dish after dish is an aesthetic surprise, you’ll be thrilled every time somebody comes to your table with so many components, all beautiful and unique. Every dish was great for us, some outstanding and the best i have ever tasted. It just keeps coming and your dopamine receptors will be in overdrive. The salty ocean, toasty grains, bitter chocolate. I get it, this is why this was number one. It will stick in my mind for a long time.

Finishing the savory with that potato, I loved. Yes it’s a single potato, that’s baked in clay. After a meal full of new things, this simple-flavored gesture but a huge tribute to the culture, was beautiful for me.

First dessert is my current favorite in the world. 

The negative reviews I understand, but if you expect to see and taste ingredients you will never get, your mind will be blown

Some improvements on staff: doing the same story, day after day, takes its toll. I totally understand you need to memorize the show and tell of so so many dishes, and it was still smooth and enjoyable, but sometimes it felt too routine. 

Go with an open mind, expect to explore some things you might like, things you love and perhaps one thing that’s too salty/bitter for you.

reviews.title: Overprice, overhyped & not enjoyable
reviews.text:
We booked Central 6 months ahead of our planned trip to Peru. It was meant to be a highlight. It certainly wasn’t. We had 16 courses with matching wines costing us $600USD ($900AUD) each. Sure it was theatre and a journey through Peru. Most wines were nearly ok, 3 “cocktails” were more scientific experiments than a cocktail & 1 beer we got barely a taste of was as the 1 bottle of beer between 2 people was whisked away - was not even barely pleasant. 
Now the food was 16 courses (some courses had 3 components - so a lot of food) - the first 8 were mainly seafood based and were not at all nice. Some were doughy and bland. The presentation was beautiful but service was rushed and we felt like we were being watched - as soon as a spoon was put down the table was cleared for the next course. By the time we got course 12 (pork course) we were so full we were wishing it to end! Save your money and have a nice meal with a top notch wine without being sucked in the hype.

reviews.title: Not quite as good as I’d hoped
reviews.text:
Visiting the 2023 #1 restaurant in the world was our main reason for visiting Peru
Whilst it was good it was a little underwhelming I thought 
It was much bigger than I imagined with two dining rooms and well over 100 covers I’d guess
This was reflected in the meal I thought
It felt like we were very much on a schedule 
For example the first course was in front us before our apéritif’s had arrived and our second course before our wine arrived
I’ve not had that before
The multiple courses were beautifully presented of course and the food was a journey through Peru
As always some dishes were excellent and some not to my taste but I can’t remember any particular dish standing out
Overall I’m glad we visited but it doesn’t make my top #5 restaurants

reviews.title: Deserves its reputation as #1 restaurant
reviews.text: We had a delicious time at Central - it deserves its reputation as best restaurant in the world! Every dish was creatively put together and reflective of the locations in Peru we visited, ranging from the ocean to the Amazon rainforest to the Andes. The wine and alcohol pairings were very well-matched to each dish. The service was extremely friendly and smooth, with great explanations of all the food. Great way to finish off our trip in Peru!

reviews.title: Experience in Central Restaurant Barrancos Lima Peru.
reviews.text: For those who enjoy molecular food and fusions of elements of the Altiplan culture, they offer a 14-step experience that runs from the bottom of the Peruvian sea to the Andes mountain range in its ingredients and preparations with a focus on sustainability.

reviews.title: Delighted with customer service.
reviews.text: Excellent attention from the team very professional and helpful, they guided us in every detail of the dishes and made us feel comfortable.

reviews.title: The most expensive restaurant in the world
reviews.text: Incredibly overpriced. $2,800 for four for dinner is an exceptionally high bill. Admittedly, it was well presented and experimentally interesting. To provide context, at 1/3 of this price, we could have had a lovely dinner at Oswalds in London which is one of the bazlar private clubs with much much better wine, much better ambiance, far superior decor and equally attentive service.  The food would be more enjoyable - perhaps less interesting! I made the reservation and was waitlisted and there was no proactive warning about the price, which I would have expected. Definitely not the best restaurant in the world, but surely up for the most expensive! Would absolutely advise anyone not to go.

reviews.title: An experience yes, but certainly not a treat
reviews.text:
Central in Lima is known to be the best restaurant in the world, so at the end of our Peru tour this was of course a must-see. And after the impressions of yesterday evening, I struggle with an assessment, because the ambience, the service, the concept - all professional and to the point. The explanations of the food as well. But did that have anything to do with pleasure? Absolutely not. The taste experience is comparable to an experimental piece of music - strange compositions alternate with slanted false tones and one wonders during the menu where the enjoyment remains. The answer: He's not coming. After 14 courses we agreed that we would not be a (!) Court would order again. Surely, in the course of our Trips through the world’s gourmet temples, we have come across some strange dishes (I remember a deconstructed tomato or a stuffed ravioli with the mouthfeel of a fish’s eye), but an entire menu without gastronomic enjoyment? That was new. Since it was at least a blessing that all the dishes were served at quite a speed that rounded off the overall experience, we took it with humor.
Conclusion: The Central is an experience but is in the wrong category, it is more in the borderline attraction area. Anyone looking for enjoyment and a nice evening with delicious food is completely wrong.

reviews.title: World’s Best Restaurant Accolades Well Deserved
reviews.text:
One of the World’s Best Restaurant is well deserved. Our 6th time here and food is still amazing.  

We first dined here when Central first made it on the World Top 50 list,  visited multiple times since whenever we are in Lima.  This is our first time back since COVID.  Food is still amazing but as with everything since COVID, prices have increased.  

Location:  Lima, Peru.  In the Barranca neighborhood.  

Parking:  Very limited parking inside restaurant.  No parking on the street outside.  Best to take Uber or taxi. 

Reservation:  Online via restaurant website.  Advance booking required.

Ambience:  Minimalist but warm and airy feeling.  Open kitchen visible from most tables in main dining room. 

Menu:  Prix Fixe Omakase menu only (same for lunch and dinner).  14 set of courses, allow at least 2.5 hrs for 2 people (longer for larger groups).  Almost all ingredients are local Peruvian and may not be familiar to those outside the country.  Diners with complex allergies or restrictions beware. 

Service:  Impeccable if a bit serious.  English or Spanish menus and staff.  

Food:  Then menu is minimalist in primarily describing the source of ingredients.  The execution is out of this world.  Just come, be surprised and enjoy the sublime and playful flavors.

reviews.title: Virgilio doesn’t love food. He loves Peru.
reviews.text: We experienced an epic and thoughtful love poem to Peru and left slightly hungry, although felt the high price was fair. Food taste was pretty good, sometimes a little heavy on the salt which is weirdly common at Michelin/World’s Best Restaurants-level restaurants, especially in Lima. Price was worth the effort they clearly put into the entire experience. Compared to other 2+ Michelin star / World’s Best 25+ restaurants, this fits right in.

reviews.title: The Most Unconventional Best Restaurant in the World
reviews.text:
How should I describe my dining experience at Central Restaurante?  I  should be honest that I have been dining at many of the top notch, multiple Michelin stars, well-rated restaurants around the world,  but none of the restaurants have wowed me with the unique, unheard of ingredients (at least to me) that probably only Chef Virgilio Martinez would personally go for an adventure to find them.  Our family had the 14-course menu, and there is not a single course that I didn't have to search online to find out the ingredients on the beautifully-printed menu. Ingredients are searched from high altitudes at above 3,000 metres in the Andes and to sub zero below Pacific Ocean.
If you look at the food pictures alone, you would never be able to figure it out the type of food you are eating.  Each course is meticulously cooked with different textures and artistically presented in original handcrafted utensils by local artists.  Central is supporting not just the culinary community, but giving the local artists a venue to showcase their talent by making plates, bowls, glasses, forks, knifes, spoon, or simply an utensil holder and handmade paper as garnish to complement the dish.  The taste is a complexity of joy and surprise, it's almost like you would find surprise by peeling layer by layer of each spoonful of food.  The staff were attentive at all times, explaining each course to show the original form of each ingredient and how it's being cooked.  They were passionate with their job, as you can see their expression with genuine interest.  
We were most impressed with the pairing of non-alcoholic drinks, because each drink is extracted from exotic fruits or even one with mushroom which is indescribable with the taste as this is something we have never tried before.  Our dining journey lasted for 4 hours, but we treasured every moment.  I have to say it's not for the regular burger patrons, as it is not designed to be that way.  Now I know how to describe this experience - It's an avant garde performing art of culinary experience!
reviews.review_tip: Go on time as it's a 4-hour experience, and traffic is bad in Lima

reviews.title: Awful food poisoning experience
reviews.text: My wife and I ate at Central on July 9.  It was one of the worst meals we have ever had.  Food being unusual doesn't necessarily mean it is good and Central is the perfect example.  Of the 18+ dishes we had, not a single one actually tasted good.  Adding to that, by the following morning my wife was in the emergency room with food poisoning from e coli bacteria, an indication of unclean food.  I was lucky- my nausea only lasted a couple days.  We've eaten at other restaurants on "best in the world" lists but never had a bad experience until this one.

Each meticulously presented dish, often accompanied by beautiful publications on recycled paper, is an explosion of flavors and a shock in the senses. Unperishable!

reviews.title: Central restaurant in Lima Peru
reviews.text: I recently dined at central restaurant in Lima, and unfortunately, it was a disappointing experience. The background music felt more suited for a spa, lacking any vibe or energy, which made the atmosphere dull and uninspiring. The food was another letdown; nearly every dish was overly creamy, leaving no room for variety or excitement. Overall, it wasn't the experience I was hoping for.

reviews.title: A pleasure for all the senses
reviews.text: The decoration that is the first thing you receive when you enter, the furniture, the sobriety of the uniforms of the staff, everything indicates order and neatness. After crossing the garden, you will be greeted by a person before a beautiful stone table with all the seeds, roots, grains, spices, and other vegetable elements that will be part of the menu. I do not remember exactly the number of dishes of the tasting but about 16, to which richer and tastier. The dishes and cutlery (to be chosen by each, of precious woods or metal, designed specifically for the restaurant also worth reviewing. It really was a very pleasant experience for all the senses. In addition, we had come with great interest after watching the documentary about its creator Virgilio Martínez and his wife Pia León, whom I had the pleasure of greeting personally.

reviews.title: Major let down...
reviews.text:
The food experience fell short of my expectations, which were admitedly fairly high. Opted for the Mundo Mater tasting menu which was said to provide a synthesis of the research and interpretation work of the Central team and this menu was specifically recommended for first time guests. The menu invites you to explore native ingredients found at 14 different altitudes throughout Peru, ranging from 10 metres below sea level to 4,200 metres above sea level, with each dish representing a particular eco-system.

PROS: Remarkable use of indigenous ingredients by a chef who is true to his stated concept. Despite one or two fails and subject to what follows, dishes were tasty and flavourful.

CONS: It is not normal for a 14-course menu to only require the use of spoons. Repettitive use of soft custardy textures in dish after dish quickly becomes boring and this lack of texture detracts from the taste. Felt I was in a test kitchen for baby food.

When all is said and done, am I glad to have had this opportunity to eat at Central? Yes. Do I agree this is the No.1 restaurant in the world? Definitely not.

reviews.title: A magical evening at Central
reviews.text:
A memorable meal.   Tastes and textures were exquisite and the food was beautifully presented on creative tableware.   I appreciated the fine crystal wine glasses which allowed the colours and aromas to shine through.    Staff too were attentive but not intrusive and service was paced perfectly - we arrived at 7:30 and left at 11:00 and hardly noticed how time had flown - unusual  for me as I’m often ready to leave restaurants well before the bill arrives.     I loved the dining room which manages to be relaxed while still feeling special .  Tables are well spaced giving a sense of having one’s own personal area.    
Dining out for me is having dishes I can’t prepare at home (I cook a lot).   Being offered ingredients that have been transformed in ways that I can’t manage myself is the USP of dining out.   And Central did all this and more.   There is a certain magic in being able to transform an uninspiring razor clam into a delectable dish - and vision too of course.    Altogether a great experience - expensive, but there is a large staff to pay.

This restaurant and food isn’t for everyone.   The food concept - altitude based - is exciting and the dishes do not conform to a palate accustomed to familiar foods.     The aim is not to provide an impeccable rendering of familiar classics but to explore savours.   So no doubt more conservative diners may find some dishes  challenging.
reviews.review_tip: Go with an open mind - go to explore.

reviews.title: Best restaurant in the world? WELL...
reviews.text: It was an "experience" - from an architectural point of view, the entire area, including the restaurant, was chosen with taste and style. The menu was interesting at first, but became very monotonous and bland as the dishes progressed. All of the dishes were bite-sized, and there was never a knife or even a need for one. Unfortunately, the combination of sea and mountains was never noticeable, as there was only one pork belly and that was not our taste. The service was monotonous, extremely quick, no smiles. The kitchen was strictly managed. All in all, not a highlight for us and we cannot recommend the restaurant. There are much cheaper restaurants in South America that also have their name, but have a combination of flavors that will stay in your memory!

reviews.title: Food poisoning from the “best restaurant in the world”
reviews.text: We dined at central on Wednesday 15th for dinner. The food made my husband violently ill with food poisoning. He had to be seen by a doctor for treatment who confirmed our suspicions of food poisoning. He had eaten dishes that I had spit out because they tasted bad, which is probably why he got sick and not me. Upon contacting the restaurant they dismissed our case and denied their fault in the matter. Considering we paid 1,450 USD for the meal, we expected to not fall ill from it. We had to cancel our plans for our last day in Peru and pay for the doctor and medicine to treat the food poisoning. Food poisoning is a serious matter and can cause extreme health problems if untreated. Do not go here if you value your health. The food presentation is pretty, the staff is attentive, the wine was good, but it is not worth your health. Central clearly does not care about their customers health or wellbeing.
reviews.review_tip: Do not eat here if you value your health.

reviews.title: Really the #1 rated restaurant in the world!
reviews.text:
Where do I begin? After eating next door at Kjolle restaurant the day before owned by Pia Leon the wife of Virgilio Martínez Veliz my expectations were already off the charts. 

Picked the Mundo menu (above and below sea level) and they took us on an adventure throughout Peru and journeyed through history with their seasons. 

Totally mind blown from start to finish. I am still thinking about how wonderful everything was and will remember this place for decades to come. 

The food, decor, presentation, staff, ambiance was just so beautiful. 

Look at my pictures to get a feel to see why they are the #1 rated restaurant in the world.

reviews.title: Lifetime food experience
reviews.text: After 7 years, back in what is now the number 1 restaurant in the world. All in all it had 7 years more charm. Nowadays it is a well-oiled machine, with fantastic dishes that are served in a very unique way. A life experience, with great flavors, that you can only experience here. From the 14 course elevation menu there are taste experiences that are excellent but also slightly less so, but that cannot be otherwise. The accompanying South American wines from Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and of course Peru were great! We enjoyed !!!

reviews.title: The best culinary experience
reviews.text: The experience is 100 percent worth it, the food is not always super tasty but it is different and the service is phenomenal.
reviews.review_tip: Es increíbles pasar horas conociendo de los ingredientes y sabores. Tuvimos la suerte de que Virgilio saliera a platicar con nosotros, mejor

reviews.title: Special experience--educational, relaxing, delightful
reviews.text:
What a special experience!  This restaurant lived-up to its reputation.

Service throughout the meal epitomized fine dining.  The dishes and drinks were served with precision and accuracy; they were described beautifully, but succinctly; and the team interacted with visitors with warmth and no hint of snobbery.  I loved the pride the team took in each element of the experience, as well as some of the conversation we got to have with them as the evening continued.  Just really special.

The setting is gorgeous--the entry experience, through a beautiful garden and into a small room with a beautiful table featuring many of the ingredients, was really neat.  The restaurant has a low-key vibe--a nice mix of rustic and modern touches--and it was easy to hear ourselves and the servers.  Yet, the space still had great energy and a nice vibe.

The beverage pairing was really interesting, featuring items beyond wine and showcasing some things produced locally.  I didn't love each sip, of course, but I really liked the variety and thought the pairings were done thoughtfully.  And I LOVED some of the sips.

The meal was about 14 courses; each course was based on an elevation and featured ingredients from that elevation, ranging from below sea level to several thousand feet.  I loved how the meal (and the entire mission of the restaurant) showcases the amazing ingredients that are native to Peru.  As you'd expect, each course was served on gorgeous stoneware, and the plating was really beautiful.

The food was excellent--across the evening, a huge variety of textures and flavors.  It was a thought-provoking meal, but also a really tasty one, with some truly outstanding bites.  

A really special evening.  Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Extremely overrated, food not that good.
reviews.text:
We fell for the hype and went to say we had been.   We wish we hadn't.

The *experience* is delightful -- the 'story' of how they are using the different Peruvian ecosystems is interesting, the service is excellent, our wine pairings were good (though, honestly, nothing amazing compared to other wine pairings we have had).

Oh, the food.  Of 14 courses ... we can't name a single one that was wonderful to eat.  They are all 'interesting' -- yeah, you're eating some bit of algae, or amazon palm ... but whether it's $100 or $1000 per couple, you want something that's just plain delightful to eat.  And honestly ... this meal failed that test.  We just didn't enjoy it -- as others have said, it's a lot of super smooth molecular gastronomy gels or foams or what-not -- very little actual tasty food.  

We were ready for it to be over an hour before we left.  Just not good.  Great story for food writers, not great food for our palate.

reviews.title: Ruined Art
reviews.text:
The experience at Central could have been an artistic experience.
The proposed route is an artistic, gustatory and visual experience accompanied by unique and surprising pottery that allows you to experience moments in which sight and taste marry wonderfully. I am an Italian artist and when I find something that creates amazement and wonder my heart fills with joy. But precisely as an artist I know that art in all its forms must be experienced in silence. It is the senses of the spectator, of those who live it that speak in an experience that sometimes touches on mysticism.
My 2 star review (I was undecided between one or two) has a question in it:
Why ruin all of Virgilio Martinez's work? Or rather, what need does Virgilio Martinez have to cover his art by distracting us?
1: The open kitchen (it seems to be trendy in Peru lately) had a blinding light. The useless shouts of the chefs (aping the Japanese but it makes sense) and their continuous banging of pots in an attempt to make a show of I don't know what sense brought me abruptly to the ground, initially causing me annoyance and then irritation. I was wonderfully traveling, flying. Why ruin the experience for me? Among other things, none of the chefs used caps or gloves. Had everyone gotten ready for the little show?
2 : The robotic service. Sometimes I looked at the waiters and wondered if they were humanoid. Cold phrases and formal smiles. Explanations from a nice little lesson learned at school. Sometimes I stopped the waiter because the noises from the kitchen didn't make me understand the words (Spanish is not my native language). The waiter seemed to short circuit. Bzzz…bzzz… He had trouble recovering.
From my culinary experience in various latest generation Peruvian restaurants it seems to me that the research and proposal of raw materials from this country is making surprising evolutions, but the service, the dining room, is still linked to an idea of servility of luxurious environments, for rich people , in which a useless and cold formality does not have the ability to evolve into a form of courtesy and attention that aims to make the guest feel at ease. A bit of heart, of cuteness, so to speak.
This attitude led to the moment in which I felt worse. The air conditioning was very high. It was very cold and the noise of the appliance competed with the noise of the cooks. I asked if it could be lowered. They replied "no, it was programmed like this". Suddenly all art shattered. I paid €600 x 2 (maybe more!) to hear an answer like this, with an irritating snobbish smile?
The ending was that we were in a hurry to finish, we were frozen, and I missed the cocoa experience. I was very sorry.
I was truly disappointed and sorry. Peruvian cuisine is making giant strides, but the service is stuck in medieval courts... including jesters.
Catering is not just cooking.

reviews.title: Overrated Restaurant in Lima
reviews.text: This has to be one of the worst experience I’ve had at a restaurant. It is, by far, the most overrated restaurant I’ve been to. It’s laughable to say that this is the #1 restaurant in the world. Let me start with the Course Menu; none of the plates were memorable. I understand that the products come from all over Peru, but where is the explosion of taste. All of the dishes had some type of cream base that was pre-made and dispensed from a metal canister onto the plate. They have an open kitchen, so you can see how the food is being prepared. I couldn’t believe what I was seeing. So disappointing, I wanted this lunch experience to be the highlight of my trip, instead it was the nightmare. We’ve been to the many top restaurants all around Lima and Europe, you can check my profile. As a matter of fact, we did the Dinner Experience at Maido a few years back and had a great experience. I knew how much this was going to cost, that is why I expected the best. Central is lot of hype that does not deliver the quality. Not a good experience, to say the least. They should advertise this place as a Museum, not a top-notch restaurant. I would not recommend this restaurant, there are countless of restaurants all around Lima that are way better. You’ll be happy skipping this restaurant.

reviews.title: A feast for the eyes but not for the palate"
reviews.text: We had the "Mundo en Desnivel Experience". which comprised of 14 courses.  Even tough each course was creatively plated, the  flavors of most dishes were too strong.  Some were so salty that left  us feeling as if we had gargle with salt water.  Others were too sweet.  The contrast between dishes was too extreme.  Either too salty or  too sweet.  Needless to say, we were quite disappointed.  I certainly hope that Chef Virgilio reads this review because he needs to do more quality control or perhaps shorten the menu to less courses.  Additionally, the service was not at the level of a 3 Michelin Star Restaurant.   We had a pile of empty glasses at our table.  It is  not the quality of service you are accustomed to find at one of the best restaurants in the world.  The wines selected  were great and the immersive experience to the different regions of Peru was a nice touch but the taste of the food did not meet our expectations.
reviews.review_tip: It is an experience but not sure if your palate will enjoy it.

reviews.title: Central Restaurant
reviews.text: My recent visit to Central, acclaimed as one of the world's top dining destinations, was filled with anticipation and intrigue. The ambiance of Central is truly enchanting, complemented by exemplary service and a detailed narrative about the origins of each ingredient, which I found both informative and engaging. Upon arrival, we were promptly seated and introduced to an innovative menu concept based on elevation and the passage of time, a unique approach that piqued my interest. The dishes we experienced were delicious, and the service was flawless, attentive without being intrusive, which added to the overall exceptional dining experience. However, despite these high points, I find myself hesitating to give Central a perfect rating. The reason lies in the value proposition; the total cost of our meal came to $1,000+ USD for my wife and me, a price point that, in my personal opinion, didn't fully match the overall experience. This has led me to the conclusion that, while Central is undoubtedly a must-visit for aficionados of exotic and high-quality cuisine, I might not find myself returning. The culinary journey at Central is undeniably of the highest quality, but it may not resonate with everyone's palate or perceived value. For those with a penchant for the exotic and a desire to explore the pinnacle of culinary craftsmanship, Central will undoubtedly be a delight. However, for me, it was a one-time experience to satisfy my curiosity, albeit a memorable one.

reviews.title: Unfortunately disappointing
reviews.text:
We had a reservation at 12.45 and were there about 10 minutes beforehand. The employees present made us and other guests wait on the sidewalk in front of the closed gate; we felt like unwelcome supplicants. They could have invited us into the beautiful courtyard to explain the delay.
We had already been to the Central a few years ago, still in the old place, and we are still delighted with the food today - especially because of the strangeness and uniqueness of the variety of flavors.
This time, unfortunately, our expectations were not met.
The waiters rattled off the menu in a careless and sometimes incomprehensible manner.
One course followed the other at lightning speed.
We all speak English and Spanish and asked several times to give us some time between courses, but unfortunately this did not happen at all. Furthermore, of the 14 courses, too many were fish and shrimp courses.
For us, the only meat course was a relief.
Overall, the amount of food was too much for everyone (a vodka had to help in between, but here too we didn't wait for the next course.)
As the number 1 in the world, we were looking forward to dessert (= everything from the cocoa bean), but it was loveless, mediocre, disappointing.
The price-performance ratio was not right at all, not even with regard to the local wine accompaniment.
Overall, a very, very shame.

reviews.title: An experience of a lifetime
reviews.text: Central Restaurant in Peru offers an unparalleled dining experience, immersing guests in a 3-4 hour culinary journey that showcases the country's vast diversity. It's a must-visit for anyone looking to explore the rich flavors and innovative dishes of Peruvian cuisine.

reviews.title: Special experience
reviews.text: I came to this restaurant in Lima, from Europe, with great curiosity. We arrived earlier. The taxi dropped off in front of the restaurant, but we thought it was in the wrong place. There was nothing to indicate that anything was here. The company sign appeared a few minutes before the opening. After a short wait, we were ushered into the forecourt. There was an exhibition, presentation and information about the raw materials. They led us to our table. The restaurant consists of several smaller and larger rooms. This allows the guests to be separated and nothing disturbs the presentation. There were six of us and 3 staff took care of us. Before each dish, the main ingredients were presented and information was given about them. We chose the 12-course lunch and the complete wine list. Many interesting flavors, colors and textures characterized the food. Although I travel the world and visit restaurants around the world, they used many ingredients that were unknown to me. I had a nice, pleasant lunch with my friends. The food was of high quality. Although this is not welcome in the case of wines. Several items there were only mid-range. The overall price of almost 700 USD is very high. Still, we didn't regret it, but we'll skip it next time...

reviews.title: We were disappointed
reviews.text:
Price-performance ratio is not right at all.
10 years ago we were totally delighted with the sensational flavors; now with 14 courses there are too many fish dishes that have already filled us up by the 5th course; better again at the end, but the impressive desserts were missing.
Overall much too expensive; our expectations unfortunately were not met; staff unfortunately professional, but uninspired, uninterested despite having the same language skills

reviews.title: It's normal that it's the best in the world
reviews.text:
Well yes, we have been one of the privileged ones to have made an appointment to try the best restaurant in the world.
One word: WONDERFUL.
There are two different types of menu. We went for the longest one, with 14 passes. And you can choose it with an independent drink, or a special pairing prepared by a Spanish sommelier. Well, nothing, lost in the river: special pairing.
From that moment on, relax and enjoy. They often change some of the preparations because sometimes it depends on the product available. What will almost not change is the extraordinary sensation in each pass, in each plate. The explanations are fantastic and allow you to enjoy the dishes and drinks much better.
The book they give away for each diner is a very nice detail (for the price you pay, it is appreciated).

reviews.title: To live once
reviews.text:
The place is very nice, upon arrival they welcome you very well and give you all the explanations about the foundation of the restaurant, then you go to the table and we chose a 12-step menu which explains everything from the ingredients to the utensils where they are served, the presentation of each step is spectacular, as for the flavors there were some that we definitely did not like but in the end it is experimental, I do not regret having gone since it is a completely different experience, but for once, I would not particularly repeat it, I caught everything its surroundings but not its flavors, expect a little more from the experience.
Attention 100
Presentation 100
Flavors of 12 dishes, 4 of which I really liked

reviews.title: A unique culinary experience
reviews.text:
So... How was my experience at Central Restaurant Lima, Peru? In a word: Unique.  I’m not one who usually forks out $500 for a meal at a fancy restaurant -but was it worth it? Totally! It's a special thing. I don't think anyone would be able to easily try and taste this mix of ingredients, textures and flavours, let alone in such an artistic and clearly beautiful manner. 

Is it for everyone? I don't think so. It’s not your average fine restaurant where you expect to eat the best pasta or meat in the world. It's an adventure. Everything was and tasted unusually nice. Of course, I liked some dishes more than others but I liked all of them. And whilst some could, very well be considered "risky", to your average or demanding palate, they all seem very well thought-through and balanced. Which leads me to: the pairing…

OMG! I'm so glad we included the drinks pairing -it took things to whole new level. The drinks themselves weren't just wines.  But also distilled and fermented drinks -all locally Peruvian made. Again, each drink quite particular in its texture and taste. I was especially surprised about the wines cause; I’ve tried a lot of wines around the world throughout my life but I hadn't experienced many “good” Peruvian wines before. Some of these drinks I would definitely never have them on their own, nonetheless paired with a specific dish -as in the experience- wow, it opens up a whole new level of flavour and texture toning.  And the glasses…

OMG! I fell in love with the crystal wine glasses! They extracted profuse aromas from the drinks. Yet so thin and fragile, clear and clean that I had to ask the waitress: “How do you wash these glasses?!”    The crockery and cutlery were also beautiful and authentic.

Now, was it an out-of-this-world experience? Specifically in the culinary part, I would say: definitely yes.  I could also be a bit naïve.  I’ve had my good share of restaurants worldwide but this was my first experience at this level and apparently my first stop has been all the way to the top.  

Hence, at this level, I would give the whole experience 8 out of 10 (or 4 out of 5).  Don’t get me wrong, everything was really good, especially in the culinary part but again at this level expectations could reach beyond human.  There’s always, and will be, room for improvement -and that’s the magic of it too, isn’t it?

The restaurant is nice, beautiful… but it could be breath-taking.  The altitude ecosystems concept is very unique but it could convey a more vivid experience through the staff.  Most of staff was super nice and attentive but they could even have qualities to take you into a vivid journey of the ecosystem experience you are meant to be delved in.  In this regard, I guess my level of excitement did not match theirs. Whilst for me it was all sheer exciting novelty, for them was routine work expected to be delivered to a certain standard: a bit scripted if you will.   Again, don’t get me wrong, the service was fine even though I could point out a few things but I don’t want to be a party pooper. 😊

All in all, I can confirm that I loved it as I’m all excited again whilst writing this review and wanting to relive the moment.  I clearly remember sitting there and feeling exactly like when you’re on a cruise and never wanting it to end.  Even after 4 hours, I could’ve sat there all afternoon and into the night.  And of course, the company contributed heaps!

reviews.title: A Perfect Dinner
reviews.text:
It is possible to have a perfect meal. We had planned for a wonderful dinner…and our exceptions were surpasses. Immediately sat in a large , somewhat spare but beautiful room. A brief explanation of the restaurants philosophy/what the meal would be, and we were off. 

Service was professional and prompt, at the same time comfortable and engaging. The pace was our pace…next course fairly promptly after we were finished, but we lingered over some courses and all worked the same. Sommelier was knowledgeable, helped us through electronic wine list and suggest 2 great bottles well with our price range. 

And the food…the food was very good to spectacular.  Courses were big enough to enjoy but not overfill. The open kitchen was fascinating to watch, all seemed to be serious yet smiling. 

Part of a great  dinner is some luck. You’re having a good day, staff all working well and everything seems to come together. But a perfect dinner…that’s a rarity and one ingredient has to be a very great restaurant. Last night, Central gave us that gift.

reviews.title: Gastronomic Experimentation
reviews.text:
With its worldwide fame, it is highly sought after. Go only if you are willing to experiment. It's not to be fed up. Particularly excellent for me.
High cost. I recommend.

reviews.title: I wish we would have liked it🥲
reviews.text:
Let's start with the good:

The entire staff 10/10! From the moment you walk in, everyone is very friendly, super knowledgeable about the dishes and the restaurant's concept, they explain absolutely everything from what dish to start with, how to mix them, their origin, the ingredients, etc.

The place is beautiful, the house where the restaurant is located is divine, the architecture, the garden that surrounds it... the presentation of the dishes is beautiful, in short, all the details are very well taken care of.

The price is high, but it is not a surprise, it is the best restaurant in the world and the prices are published on their page, so those who book have this information in advance and there is nothing to complain about.

As for the portions, it is no surprise that they are small, you have to be clear that it is a tasting menu and if you are a friend of the "all you can eat" this is not your type of restaurant. For us who eat little, the portions were perfect and in accordance with what is normally seen in this type of restaurants. There are 12 dishes and you are satisfied.

Now the bad thing: the flavor should be the protagonist and it is not.

From the 12-course menu we can rescue 3 dishes that tasted good, we also tried the non-alcoholic pairing and 2 drinks were rescued. That is, we liked 25% of what we ate😬

I don't want to blame Central, in fact, the mistake was ours... if we had better informed ourselves and searched on the internet before booking, we would have seen that their chef has mentioned that it is not a Restaurant but a laboratory-restaurant and that their chef What he says: "You don't come to Central to eat delicious food, (that) would greatly limit all other sensations. You come here to travel and that's enough" and it couldn't be more true, it's a trip! The textures, the degree of sophistication of the dishes is impressive, we must also keep in mind that in the framework of a laboratory there is room for experimentation, even if the result is not the desired one.

We are not much of a reviewer, but because of the above we are encouraged to write this review as a warning to newcomers and with everything said, there is no room for surprises for future interested parties...

But the most delicate issue was that being in the restaurant when there were already 2 or 3 dishes left to finish the service we felt bad (stomachically) and without wanting to be very eschatological we ended up in the restaurant's bathroom.

Before writing this review I took the time to search the internet for other opinions and to my surprise I found that people get sick after eating at this restaurant, but even more surprising was to see that the restaurant has told them that it is normal when you travel that you You can get sick and of course, travel sickness is well known among world travelers, which is usually caused by drinking plain water or milk, but it is precisely avoided in that same way: by avoiding its consumption.

Just to clarify, we have had the opportunity to travel a lot around the world, we have eaten in other award-winning restaurants around the world and we have never gotten sick to the extent of this experience, but beyond this, I believe that there is a pattern for which restaurant should show interest or curiosity and not relate it to a specific situation of the origin of a diner.

To make matters worse, we have been in Peru for 10 days and have eaten in varied places from several very good restaurants in Lima, to more humble restaurants in Nazca, Paracas and small towns in Cusco where one would assume that the risk of poisoning is higher and we did not get sick. 🙃.

In conclusion and with all the pain in my heart, we do not recommend it, we were very disappointed in the flavors and worried about not knowing the cause of the stomach upset.

I admire the chef and his team for their courage, their hard work and their innovative genius. It is an honor to have the best restaurant in the world on our continent, but this one, despite holding this title, I would not recommend to any friend just for the fear of getting sick.

We are not expert palates like those of the Restaurant magazine that gave it the award, but from our humble opinion, food, no matter how innovative it may be, must always respond to the maxim of satisfying the sense to which it is directly related: taste! and unfortunately some dishes are inedible and this goes beyond the issue of particular preferences, it is a matter of flavor and the mixture between the ingredients.

I wish we had liked it.

reviews.title: Poisoned
reviews.text: We had food poisoning. Do not recommend. I read an article regarding the chef bringing ingredients illegally. The food is not up to our standard. Wine pairing was good.

reviews.title: It wasn't the best for us :(
reviews.text:
My husband I dined at Central last night and were very much looking forward to it, flying to Lima from the United States for one night before visiting other parts of Peru (Atacama and Amazon). We are not wealthy by any means, so this was a big deal to us as we had to save a lot to be able to eat here. The food concepts and creations were amazing and the staff was very friendly for the most part. Our bill was $960 USD (with tip) for the food and one glass of their least-expensive wine each. By far the most we've ever spent on a meal for two people.

We were seated when we arrived and noticed other customers being shown something at a table by the entrance. We asked about it and they were surprised that we were not given the demonstration. It was a discussion on the food concepts from different parts of the country and the different ingredients. Why did we have to ask to see this when others were being shown automatically? We sometimes notice discrimination throughout the world as a same-sex couple, but didn't expect that here. It may have simply been an oversight, but it was a little surprising, especially considering how much we were paying for the experience and how their high rating (#1 in the world).

The food was interesting and unique and I respected everything about what we were being served, although we couldn't fully understand what was being described. I still really appreciated it all though.

As we were eating, we noticed they were a little stingy with the water for some reason. I was very thirsty, but felt like I needed to ration my water as we seem to only be given maybe 5 swallows or so per course. Perhaps that had something to do with how we were experiencing the food? Not sure.

Unfortunately, after course 10 or so (of 14), my husband's stomach began to feel upset and he ended up running to the bathroom to be sick. He returned to the table and tried to eat more, but could not do it and had to get outside to get some air. We just needed to leave. I asked to quickly get the check (which, like I said, came to $960) and it took more than 20 minutes. He was waiting outside for me so we could return to the hotel.

He was sick all night, which resulted in us missing our tour the next morning for the Atacama Desert, Ballastas Islands, and flying over the Nazca lines, another experience we'd been saving for for months. His fear of being sick wouldn't allow him to do any of that.

We're now at our Lima hotel as he's trying to recover, wasting our vacation time. With our meal and missing our tour, we're out over $1500 USD which is a LOT of money to us.

Like I said, I completely appreciate the restaurant and love the fact that it exists, but unfortunately our experience there was not the best. :(

reviews.title: Worth Every Penny for an Admirer. Special Occassion Dining.
reviews.text:
My friends and I came to Peru to hike the Inca Trail, but knew there would be amazing food experiences in Lima. At the time of planning, Central was #2 on the list, but became #1 as our trip approached. I knew full well how much it would cost, and knew this was not just about the food. It is the whole experience - ambience, story, intention, and purpose.  Our interest definitely started with Virgilio’s episode on Chef’s table.  Not everything is supposed to taste amazing - but everything has an intention, everything is deliberate.  I think the idea of exploring Peru’s foods through different altitudes is so novel. Knowing all of this, how can you have expectations commensurate with a cost of the meal? 

My friends and I spent 4 wonderful hours at Central.  The hours passed like they were minutes.  We came in a good mood, open to what would be offered, we had great company in each other, and we interacted with everyone who served us - nothing tired or pretentious in our opinions.  

Even with 14 courses (the dessert courses are combined and we got an extra dessert for my birthday), each one was plentiful, with multiple bites. I was never hungry in-between, nor too full to move on.  My two friends opted for the wine pairings - the pour was plentiful.  We ordered coffee towards the end and Gerald eventually started to offer me non-alcoholic drinks to pair with my courses.  

Ambience inside is serene, sterile to some extent (not necessarily a bad thing) - but it felt like I was in a nice office/study setting.  The outdoor area is light and airy and features gardens where I presume they source some of their ingredients from.  

We were each given a book of illustrated art of Peruvian resources by Peruvian artists, a keepsake from our experience. 

My favorite courses were the Dry Valley (900 MASL) shrimp/loche squash/avocado, the Warm Sea Current (15 MBSL) grouper/razor clams/vongole, and the desserts Moray (3600 MASL) cabuya/muña leaf/qolle.

I wouldn’t come back again because the experience was unique and perfect in itself - 5 stars for this one-time culinary adventure.

reviews.title: Best of the world
reviews.text: This one lives up to the title of best in the world, the food, the wine pairing and the impeccable service

reviews.title: Innovative proposal
reviews.text:
It is a place where you live an experience that is the result of an effort to research indigenous ingredients from the sea through the Andean zone to the Peruvian Amazon. Give us the 14-course tasting menu with wine pairings.
It deserves to be number one in the top fifty.
Just one detail that is out of the ordinary on these sites; In the last dishes (desserts) on the menu, we felt pressure to speed up our departure since there were no more tables occupied and we were the last.

reviews.title: Central: A Gastronomic Experience That Defies Expectations
reviews.text:
Central, Virgilio Martínez's restaurant, far exceeded my expectations during my recent visit. Although initially it was difficult for me to understand the culinary proposal when reading the menu, the experience turned out to be exceptional. I understood why Central is ranked first in “The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2023.”

Virgilio Martínez is a culinary genius who has taken cooking to an unmatched level. Her innovative approach and the way she highlights local ingredients is amazing. Each dish is a masterpiece that challenges the norm and transforms food into a scientific experience.

Central is much more than a restaurant, it is a sensory journey that explores the diversity of Peruvian cuisine and redefines haute cuisine. My visit was transformative and it's no surprise that Central tops the list of the best restaurants in the world. Virgilio Martínez has elevated gastronomy to an unimaginable level, and I feel fortunate to have been part of this unique gastronomic experience.

reviews.title: Excellent, exquisite, refined, welcoming
reviews.text:
I was very lucky to fall in love with a Peruvian and begin to get to know their culture and gastronomy and there was no turning back in my life.
For my birthday, Dani gave me a meal at the best restaurant in the world, CENTRAL in Peru.
So we prepared our trip to Lima and although it doesn't surprise me that they are the best because of the incredible variety of products, they amply prove it.
As soon as we arrived, one of their valets (you have a great team, Virgilio) left us a hundred soles, because we forgot to bring national currency in cash to pay for the taxi.
They accompanied us inside where they explained the restaurant's philosophy and the different products we would find.
The perfect table, spectacular decoration and environment.
In fact, we came from temperatures of 35 degrees and they very kindly regulated the climate and left me a baby llama blanket so that I would be absolutely comfortable. Thank you!
They explain each dish and each drink, the region and the way of preparation.
The charming waiters, always concerned about our well-being and getting involved with us.
The dishes are a spectacle of presentation, of flavor, words could not describe the sensations of that perfect combination of products from each region and heights of Peru.
When we had finished, a special surprise arrived for me with a congratulations, what a nice detail, thanks to the waitress who I told that it was my birthday, in August!!
Details that made us fall in love.

Spanish and Peruvian, lovers of food and good wines, we have the advantage of being able to enjoy the best chefs and restaurants in the world here in Spain.
But CENTRAL and all of Peru in general is incredible, I love Peruvian food.
A more than deserved position, thank you very much Virgilio Martínez and his entire team, we will repeat for sure!

reviews.title: Terrible customer service
reviews.text: I wanted to give my brother, who is visiting Peru, the wonderful experience of dining at this restaurant that recently won the Michelin Star as the best restaurant in the world. However, not all reception staff are trained to serve the public in a cordial and respectful manner. He was informed that he could come today, October 24, 2023 at 7 pm because there would be availability of a table in room 3 for people who had not made a reservation previously. He wanted to confirm his reservation by phone but no one answered. Upon arrival, he was treated very disrespectfully and even rudely by one of the 2 girls who were receiving the diners. He tried to explain that he was there because they informed him at noon that there would be availability for dinner and although he waited for more than half an hour because they told him that they were going to check, they left him standing and when he tried to finally ask if he could have dinner , this lady treated him very badly and practically kicked him out of the restaurant. He says that the guards showed more politeness than not even this lady in charge of welcoming them. While Virgilio Martinez works like crazy to be the best chef in the world, this bitter and rude woman leaves such a poor image of Central, not only for Colombia but for the entire world. It's good that he, a tourist in Peru, is staying in Miraflores, where there are hundreds of excellent restaurants for a fraction of the 1,400 soles he was going to pay there. See you never Central, how sad it makes me Virgilio

reviews.title: Very good - but worth $650? probably not.
reviews.text: The food was delicious I loved the goat neck, deconstructed Cacao and the zucchini was fantastic. They did a an excellent job with the presentation work.  - I've eaten in similar restaurants including his wife's restaurant Kjolle, and Travail in Minneapolis as well as other James Beard/Michelin stared restaurants, Central is very good but it really isn't "great" especially at the price point they are at. Everything from the food to the staff feels like a worn out dance of wash & repeat offerings. You can tell from the staff they're tired of saying the same things to the 100+ guest they sling thru the restaurant every day. The service was tedious and slow. No one has their heart in their work - just going thru the motions.

reviews.title: McDonalds is better
reviews.text: Surprised that several restaurants in llima rank in the list of the best restaurants in the world! There must be corruption! If you like to eat 2 or 3 salad leaves and a drizzle of tasteless sauce...

reviews.title: What disillusionment!
reviews.text:
With great effort we were able to reserve a table at the number 1 in the world. Happy of course! But what a disillusionment.
Eight people of us were placed at an uncomfortable long marble table outside the actual restaurant. The air conditioning was so high that half of our party quickly had to bundle up with scarves and cardigans. Various complaints to the service did not help and eventually there was the arrival of 'the boss'. Hopeful expectations, but it remained ice cold

The 12 course menu we got was reasonable, but not more than that. What exactly we ate remains a question mark because the young waiter was unintelligible in both English and Spanish and when we asked for more information we were told the same thing again. There was no more information.

None of us are unfamiliar with good restaurants, but both the entourage and the service are far below the level of the many good restaurants in Lima.
And that for a price tag of almost 350 euros per person makes the dream of eating at the number 1 in the world a great disillusionment.

reviews.title: Happy birthday!!!
reviews.text: When we talk about Central we talk about experience, harmony of flavours, raw materials sourced from indigenous territories that are very distant and different from ours. You can't say it's good or not so good, you eat well or not so well, you eat little or a lot, it's better or worse than. The experience is sensorial and if you are not open to new experiences, there is a risk of dissatisfaction. The textures, flavours, aromas are so many that there is no reference to our flavors and textures. From my point of view it is an experience worth having. A little expensive, but if you can, why not.
