reviews.text: The theme of organizing dishes by altitude is a fun one but does it make for a great meal? Overall an expensive triumph of form over substance. A shame since the idea works much better at the tokyo sister  restaurant Maz.

reviews.title: Good experience, a little slow
reviews.text:
Definitely the place is a total experience, but it seems to me that for us Peruvians having so much delicious food. It's a little overrated for what it is.
The experience is still fantastic and so is the attention!

reviews.title: Gastronomic experience designed from start to finish
reviews.text:
Everything very well thought out. Incredible environment. Very tasty menu, unlike anything else. The gastronomic experience is really worth it. Very approachable chef, visited all the tables.
My husband paired it with wine and loved it.
The only low point was my pairing with juices - very strange juices, they were more of an experiment than actually palatable. If you can consume alcoholic drinks, choose the wine menu.
Very expensive and requires reservations well in advance, so plan ahead.

reviews.title: Excellent experience
reviews.text: We went in pairs and it was an experience from start to finish. From how they explain the inputs and ingredients to the flavors and service, everything is excellent. The truth is that, if it does not cause you a personal/family financial problem, it is completely worth it, it is a totally different experience that you have to do once in your life. The only thing that left me a little disappointed was that the portions, even though there were 10, left us hungry. For those who are going for the first time, go with the mentality that you will not leave satisfied. Other than that, 100% recommended.

reviews.title: An experience but a disappointing and expensive one!
reviews.text:
I did struggle writing this review. As the number one rated restaurant in the world, this restaurant will always split opinions. It certainly split my family’s. My wife loved it. My own and my son’s view is that some of the dishes were very good, others less so with style winning over substance, with far too many being of the deconstructed type which in my view just ruins the taste and experience. Unfortunately and very disappointingly there was not a single dish that stood out as outstanding. This should not distract from the ingenuity and creativity of the team at Central, but I feel they are trying way too hard  with the result being that the flavours of the ingredients simply do not shine. 

The concept here is an experience in itself. The restaurant beautiful. The staff very friendly and thoroughly knowledgeable as they should be. However, I had requested (though forgot) a 12 course meal but was provided a 14 course. Also ended up taking a wine pairing which was given as a choice of either European or South American (though no menu was provided). I chose the South American, which they explained would be wine, cocktails, beer or cider - rather unique and certainly all the pairings worked well with the dishes. 

Was it worth paying nearly £1,000 for this - no it was not. A lot of these ‘high-end’ restaurants offer only experience menus, but fail to deliver on what really matters - letting the underlying ingredients shine. They need to go back to their roots and reconsider their approach. There are many talented chefs doing wonderful things who they could learn from.

reviews.title: A gastronomic center
reviews.text: I was worried. The day before I had dinner at Mayta and the experience didn't entirely satisfy me. I found a lot of food, a lot of different dishes and not necessarily good ones. I thought it could be more of the same and never hear about Peruvian food again. But I was pleasantly surprised. In the main hall there are only 11 tables. Glazed kitchen. Sober but pleasant atmosphere. It looks like a gastronomic laboratory. The attendants circulate around the tables presenting each of the 14 steps. All very good. Interesting wines accompanied each dish, although the sommelier was the least friendly in the place. I don't know if he deserves to be chosen number 1 in the world, but it's certainly a great experience. It's worth the cost (3000 soles per couple, something like 4000 reais).

reviews.title: Central Lima: a… painful experience!
reviews.text:
Ah! Le Central de Lima, voted best restaurant in the world in 2023, which welcomes us with a smile, then reassures us about my wife's seafood allergy, and its ability to take her too into the delights of a journey of tasting curious and often exquisite dishes.
The magic happens despite the feeling, sometimes, of being faced with robotic servers, repeating in algorithmic loops the presentation of “levels of experience”; despite the impression, also, of a much inferior preparation of my wife's dishes compared to the original dishes, almost all based on marine products.
Then comes the time to pay the bill for the trip, and the charm suddenly dissipates: 60% more expensive than the price communicated when booking a few months previously!!
The worst, servers still as robotic, but in aggressive mode now, who protest at my astonishment and my criticism regarding the total absence of information: it was my responsibility to check the updated prices on the site, and the restaurant does not, at any time, have to communicate about these kinds of “details”…
A farce, a scandal: how to be taken from 400 dollars without having a say, or having to pay around 1000 dollars for what was supposed to cost 600!!
Another baseness: making my wife pay for the harmonization of the dishes with the wine when she does not drink, as I had indicated to the waiter, and just dipped her lips twice in the wine glass during the entire meal.
To top it off: being forced to spend a painful amount of time making transfers to my card account, in order to be able to pay the hefty bill - and abusive, above all - under the annoyed gaze of hermetic servers at any remarks and any empathy.
They are undoubtedly used to snobbish customers, full of money, who like to pay without even looking at the bill. Sorry, I'm a different type, enthusiastic about tasting the best food in the world, but aware of the value of things and careful about spending.
Moreover, it was 3:30 p.m., the kitchen had already closed, and the obvious became clear: the Central Lima staff wanted me to pay as quickly as possible and leave without asking for my rest.

A bad experience, unfortunately: the Central de Lima deserves its place, perhaps, among the best restaurants in the world because of its culinary creativity – I cannot say this as I am not a specialist -, but it positions itself, without a doubt, in the world top ranking of establishments which abuse their customers, make colossal price changes without deigning to communicate and, in the end, extort amateur gourmets without hesitation.

reviews.title: Incredible experience
reviews.text: Truly amazing experience at Central. This is the best restaurant in the world for a reason. Absolutely perfect tasting journey, with all the best of Peru on the table. Dishes prepared to perfection and ingredients treated with skill. Impeccable service with explanations and maximum attention to the customer. Spectacular location. Price obviously in line with the quality of the experience.

reviews.title: Exaltation of Peruvian ecosystems
reviews.text:
The impact upon arrival at the Central is almost like a modern art gallery, a lot of marble and stone, but not a strictly cold and aseptic atmosphere. On the contrary.
After a brief description of the native products used in the menu, accompanied to your table, the experience of this highly acclaimed restaurant begins.
Dishes that surprised me quite a bit, not only for the taste, but perhaps because I was simply expecting them to be more "cerebral".
In reality, the concept of this menu exists and is very present, tangible, much more than the majority of gourmet restaurants: the total use of mountain, or Amazonian, or coastal products, but in any case exclusively Peruvian.
In particular I appreciated clams in two marinades: with algae and spirulina, and with lemon oil and ash; pumpkin stuffed with prawn bisque with foam and ash from the pumpkin itself; Andean potato cooked in a miniature oven of salt, clay and herbs; paiche ceviche with watermelon and coca oil sauce.
All the dishes were excellent, in my opinion a little weaker in the desserts, but overall a coherent menu closely linked to the territory.
Excellent service and I also found good value for money in the wines.
From a conceptual restaurant like this I would have expected the absence of cocktails during lunch (which I hate as they alter the flavours), but in reality it is a widespread practice everywhere and in South America in particular.

reviews.title: Worst best restaurant in the world with big chance for food poisoning
reviews.text:
This spot is great if you want to get food poisoning which is exactly what we got and quite severe after our lunch there. 
Great experience but if you dont want to risk getting sick better to avoid this restaurant due to the risk they take with raw ingredients

reviews.title: The World’s #1 Culinary Experience of 2023
reviews.text: We had the pleasure of dining at Central in June of 2023, right when it was named the #1 restaurant in the world. Central isn't your typical high-end restaurant, but rather a holistic experience for the senses. From the moment you walk in, there is a table which showcases all of the ingredients that you will be consuming. Ambiance wise, the calming meditative music helps you to truly focus your senses. Their tasting menu takes you on a journey through the different regions of Peru. For instance, the first dish will have you begin in the Amazon, followed by the second dish on the coast, the third in the Andes Mountains and so on. The restaurant truly goes out of their way to show you exactly what you will be eating and where those ingredients are coming from. Their ultimate mission is for you to understand the complex culinary regions of Peru through different microclimates. The dish that stood out to us the most, was their disassembled Cacao dessert. They place a large Cacao fruit on the table and showcase a dessert platter which utilizes each part of the plant. We highly recommend you reserve Central during your trip to Lima. It is a perfect way to highlight each part of Peru through a culinary experience.

reviews.title: Central restaurant Peru can’t justify
reviews.text: The cost. Does not justify the quality, quantity or overall experience of the place. If you want to brag that you are at a place that got no 1 globally go. But you can experience 200 Peruvian places equally for 25% of the cost or less.  The story they tell is common knowledge and can get from any place or cooking class in Peru. Sorry but not justified for the cost.

reviews.title: Romantic journey through the very construct of the Peruvian nation.
reviews.text:
This was our sixth visit to Central and, like all previous ones throughout the years, it did not disappoint. Whilst the early years with an à la carte menu were about traditional execution of great dishes, the move to a fixed menu and the work done in capturing the very complex flavours and history of a country bring an entirely different focus. 

To me, this is not at all about judging food in the way a typical Michelin experience would suggest it. The Central experience, which over the years has gained in maturity and standard, is really about an almost romantic discovery of the Peruvian nation, its ecosystems and the people who make them breath and come to life. The work done through Mater Iniciativa is of course pivotal here, as a deep focus on recording and preserving native fauna and flora. 

So coming here to be fed is almost certain to be a disappointment - forget portion size, forget the construct of traditional dishes and embrace what is an extremely well crafted journey around Peru. 

To be constructive, the staff was of very mixed quality - the waitress assigned initially to our table was fairly mediocre, with a limited ability to engage. This changed greatly when sommelier Cristian took over for a fantastic dive into some of the terroirs of Peru. Reservation manager Carla was, as always, super efficient. 

The price makes little sense if compared to any other restaurant in Peru (or in many other places) but then again no other restaurant in Peru or elsewhere is built on such a detailed research on the very essence of a country. As such, this makes Central a must stop for every visit to Lima and for anyone interested in an almost mystical journey through a land we only now start to catalog and learn from.

reviews.title: Overhyped and overpriced for very mediocre experience and food
reviews.text: Terrible waste of time and money. The food was not exceptional as most of the courses were not worthwhile or enjoyable. One course was a scrawny, tasteless, dried up potato. Not certain how this is considered a top restaurant. We will never return to this disappointing restaurant.

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.text: The food is so untasty: flavors unbalanced and it’s so gimmicky. Most of the people there are Americans. Quite overpriced and underwhelming

reviews.title: Amazing meal at Central
reviews.text: Had an amazing experience at Central. From the initial welcome to the very end service was beyond outstanding. Each course came with it’s own unique story, and everything tasted amazing. We were continually surprised and delighted throughout the evening. The space is gorgeous as well. Definitely expensive, but well worth it!

reviews.title: Number one restaurant for 2023
reviews.text: On my list for a few years now. In every city, there is at least one place where you would like to dine and for different reasons. Central has a reputation for being unique in its approach to designing the menu. Peru is a country of altitudes and a diversity of produce which are clearly presented in the menu. The place itself is beautiful with a view of the kitchen. Super professional and friendly staff who make sure that everything and every moment is perfected. We chose the 12 altitudes with a non alcoholic pairing. A delight, to the eyes, the nose and the palate. Twelve is an understatement as several steps were made up of several dishes. Words are not enough to describe the experience. It was delicious, exciting and entertaining. I also loved all the plates and the bowls and the beautiful cutlery in all its forms. Thank you for a memorable experience and a dinner that we will remember for a long time. Congratulations for getting the number one spot in the 50 best👏. A very well deserved award. Thank you Virgilio and Pia.

reviews.title: Good to try once, but that’s enough
reviews.text:
First, it took a lot of trouble to make a reservation at this restaurant. My friend was raving about the concept and how unique the experience is. So I guess many also shared this excitement and thus the restaurant gets booked up really early. After many attempts to secure a table, only to find the online payment link didn’t work. Alas I finally got it done and was really looking forward to the experience. 

Unfortunately our flight from Cusco was delayed by 4 hours. I notified the restaurant while waiting anxiously at the departure lounge, only to be told curtly that they would only accommodate a half hour delay, nothing more. We were fully expecting to miss the reservation, but our driver and guide were so kind to speed through Lima Saturday night traffic and got us there in the nick of time (and then took our luggage to hotel so we could checked in after dinner). 

Upon arrival, I was kind of expecting quite a lot of “attitude” given all the commotion with the booking and timing of arrival. But there was none. It was all smiles, from the entrance to being seated to being offered menu and drinks. Service was friendly, attentive, patient (given there was a lot of explaining to do). Of all things I would give top marks to waiting staff service. 

Okay, then came the experience. It was indeed very unique, to taste different aspects of Peruvian cuisines based on different altitudes and climates. Given the wonderful culture of the country, it does provide fascinating backdrop to curate the cuisine and that is a new perspective that we have never seen. The staff meticulously explained the concept of each course, plus the ingredients. It was a very “educational” dinner. As for the food itself…. Well I would be generous and give it a four star. Admittedly the hype precedes the substance, not to mention the dinner is priced on par with any 2/3 Michelin star restaurants in London and New York!

reviews.title: SCAM! Save your money
reviews.text: Two people 12 course selection, one beer and one wine selection was over $700 USD. We kept hearing about a food experience but the only experience I felt was being ripped off by a scam. Being served foam and a single potato no bigger than your thumb are some of your "courses" you receive. I felt that what you are really paying for is extravagant silverware and presentation for sub par food. Would never do it again for a fraction of the cost. Save your money and go to another restaurant where you don't leave hungry.

reviews.title: An experience beyond just eating
reviews.text: I did the elevations tasting with the paired juices. The food was all amazing and it was truly an interesting experience. They changed the tasting for me as I have a shellfish allergy and the substitutions were great. The whole thing is very detailed and involved, from the presentation to what the food is served on, it's all about senses and textures.

reviews.title: It really depends.
reviews.text:
After seeing Chef's Table I understood and liked the idea of a menu that features ingredients from all over Peru and it's different altitudes, highlighting the natural recourses Peru has to offer and supporting locals. In reality it did not match my expectations. I think there was a bit too much deconstructed food concepts and immulsions, I enjoyed the old-fashioned clay-baked potato and the piece if white fish the most. However, the staff was friendly and you could look straight into the kitchen which is always fun. The head chef took the time to talk to people which is very nice and attentive. They really tried to present an experience and a story so a lot of thought and effort went into the concept.
Personally I think it was a bit overpriced for how much I enjoyed the food.

reviews.title: Michelin Starsssss!
reviews.text: An amazing experience all around! Go ahead and try full course and wine pairing...nothing like it. Make sure to reserve well ahead. Loved it!

reviews.title: Big disappointment
reviews.text: I love food, and had looked forward to visit Central. What a disappointment. Terrible food. I could not finish any of the many dishes. We seriously considered leaving after dish three.

reviews.title: Expensive but memorable
reviews.text: The food was an experience in itself, with a tonne of new flavours and ingredients. It is a memorable meal without a doubt!

reviews.title: Noel Decàn review of Central in Lima
reviews.text: I closed my gastronomy tour of Lima by having dinner at Central, after doing so in Maido & Astrid & Gaston. It was an unique experience. I ate from the Menu instead of the 17 Course Fix Dinner representing all the levels in altitude of food source in Peru. My dinner was excellent. Started with a sophisticated salad spiced with rare herbs collected by Chef Martinez and his sister in their trips to country side. Next had tenderloin with various kind of potatoes of different colors. Delicious!  A cup of a Carmenere wine paired perfectly with my dinner. A sub-Chef was Venezuelan and kindly allowed me a photo with them in the kitchen. I highly recommend to have dinner at Central when visiting Lima, just make sure to make reservation at least 2 months in advance.

reviews.title: Disappointed and Shocked.
reviews.text: Overpriced and grandiose baby food. Certainly the chef has made an effort to bring obscure and unique ingredients from many regions of Peru. Conceptually sounds great; however they have puréed every single course into and overpriced, bland purée . After several courses the lack of texture and variation of the ingredients leave you thinking that it all tastes a little bit like Gerbers puréed vegetable baby foods. The dessert was horrendous and some of the courses were overpowering leaving you no taste of the ingredients. The wine selection was great, the non alcoholic pairings were mediocre. This restaurant is and exercise pretentiousness and over trying. Avoid this $330 meal Ina city full of delicious and unique restaurants.

reviews.title: A Sublime Experience
reviews.text: Beautifully presented food showcasing the biodiversity of Peru.  Fourteen courses delivered with impeccable service.  Fun to watch the chefs create through the glassed in kitchen.  The serving pieces, cutlery and dishes were works of art.  Garden at the entrance is lovely.  An unforgettable meal (though price is high).

reviews.title: Many mixed feelings after our lunch at Central
reviews.text:
After discovering Central on line and reading so many wonderful reviews and feeling that the quoted price for 14 tasting dishes was pricey but reasonable, I booked a date.  Yes it was interesting, over the top with servers, and personal to “wow” and all the beautiful people who were there to be wowed, and be seen. Very pretentious.
But we were good sports, went along even added an extra tip,  2,200 Sol.total. Much more than I remembered being quoted for two people. Afterwards, feeling  we’ve taken to the cleaners.  I’ve resolved this feeling or conclusion of being robbed by recognizing that when we travel, it’s inevitable that we’re going to be robbed now and again. That’s how I feel,

reviews.title: Just amazing. Great concept. Fantastic Food.
reviews.text:
After a whirlwind fortnight touring around, I ended my final night in Peru in true style by having dinner at Central. 

Having witnessed some of the different parts of this beautiful country and seeing how different and varied it can be, I felt well-placed to appreciate Central’s concept of presenting their menu in the form of different ecosystems found around the country from which it has drawn its ingredients.

The first course of 3 bite size starters of seaweed, clams and squid were all very interesting and served to whet the appetite and interest for what is to come. I couldn’t wait.

The second course of shrimp and loche squash again felt like 2 halves. I did enjoy it though, particularly the squash half which had some pieces in there that taste more the texture of fruit than a squash, which I really liked. I could have happily had a larger prawn portion, which was gone before I had the chance to form a strong impression.

The potato dish that came next was interesting. Made from the papa voladora, there were 2 forms, both surprisingly light. I was not a big fan of the dark treacly looking dip, which I thought was too sweet, but when mixed with the blobs of blue, yellow & white around it, actually made it quite pleasant.

Dish number 4 was when the menu really sprung to great heights. Corn. During my 2 weeks journeying around Peru, I hadn’t really had many good corn dishes which was surprising for a land that adores corn. This really made up for it. Packed full of flavour, it tasted like a hug when you got home after a difficult day. Warm, nourishing, heartfelt. Brilliant. There are various bits added for textures which were fine, but that liquid gold at the bottom of the bowl that was a true star.

The grouper came next, and what a pretty dish it was. I love blue, but not many foods are naturally blue, so the carefully placed strands of razor clams over the grouper made my heart & my eyes sing. The fish itself was cooked perfectly with a crispy and light batter. It was a good dish, but I was still coming down from the high of the previous dish, and I don’t think this quite scaled the same heights.

Scale the heights, the arapaima dish did. I have to admits that I didn’t quite hear everything the waiter explained about the dish and it was certainly not the prettiest. It was however definitely the tastiest. The firm texture of the flesh swimming in that flavoursome broth. Delightful and satisfying. 

The seafood extravaganza continues with a scallop dish. Scallops have to be one of my favourite things, especially if prepared well and you can taste the naturally sweetness of them. You could certainly taste that here, and I was oddly addicted to the tangy dressing even though I felt overall the tang was just a fraction too much. 

We have the octopus next. Another sea ingredient that I love, though I’m not supposed to have it too often as it causes my gout to flare. The pieces here were cooked beautifully so that it was soft, but still had a bit of chew. One of my top gripes in restaurants is when the kitchen feel the need to go heavy on the salt in order to give the food flavour. There is other ways to impart flavour. This was the only dish where I felt there was heavy-handed seasoning. Only fractionally so mind you, but the fact I noticed it is more down to how beautifully tuned the rest of the menu was.

Another potato dish for the next course. Why not, we are in the land of over 4000 potato varieties. I loved the overall presentation, even if the waiter had a bit of a struggle to open up the “shell” at the table and the potato ended looking like a shrivelled finger. The eating was not quite as exciting as the presentation but was certainly fine enough.

One of the things I don’t much like is fruit with my savouries, so I viewed the pacu & watermelon with suspicion. However, I really didn’t need to worry, this was clever and light and never veered onto the wrong side of balance of sweet and savoury. It might have also helped that watermelon is one of my top 3 favourite fruits. 

The only truly meaty dish was the pork belly. This was a touch too sweet for me to enjoy as a savoury. I kept thinking I was eating char siu with a sweet glaze. Not my favourite, but if I’m being generous, maybe the sweetness here was to prepare me for the dessert part of the menu, but I would rather have entered dessert on the back of a mighty savoury punch.

The first 2 desserts were served together and meant to be tried separately and then enjoyed together. The first part was earty and a little tart, and the second was icy and a tiny bit bitter. I think it probably eat better together than separately, but it’s not a dessert I would have chosen on an a la carte menu.

So thankfully we end on the cacao. The 7 components all made from the different parts of the bean. It was so yummy and fulfilling. The only problem was that it wasn’t a larger portions. I could certainly get used to the idea of ending ever meal with a chocolate tea. Yum yum yum.

All this comes at a bit of a hefty price of course. But I very much enjoyed the experience and was very glad to have had it. A beautiful way to round out my fortnight in Peru. As a single guy solo traveler, I sometimes feel like restaurants never quite know what to do with me, the gaps between courses sometimes feels too long, and the interaction between waiting staff and me seem more functional than tables with couples. However, here it was faultless. The service was impeccable and it felt there was a warmness all the times. Also, since I booked this dinner 3 months ago, the price has gone up, maybe due to the fact it has risen to #2 on the list of The World’s 50 Best Restaurant, but I was most delighted they charged me the price at the time of my booking. How amazing.

reviews.title: A spectacular experience
reviews.text: It is impossible to convey the level of excellence that Central provided in a simple review. The setting was sublime, attention to detail unparalleled, and quality of the fare truly exceptional. The tasting menu is a culinary adventure through Peru that mirrors its dramatic environment. The paired drinks menu is also an exploration of South America. Eating at Central is performance art with every offering stretching the imagination. Food creativity taken to new heights. An unforgettable experience from one the worlds very best restaurants.

reviews.title: A Unique Culinary experience.... Food made art....
reviews.text: The tasting menu created by Chef Virgilio Martinez will take you through a difficult to describe journey of flavors,  Colors and textures using the most exotic ingredients of Peru.... This is a unique experience that you should not miss in Lima... of course it is key to make the reservation with enough anticipation....

reviews.title: Overrated perhaps?
reviews.text: We visited Central in mid-year 202 with a group of younger colleagues.  While we ere impressed with the service and performance, we were disappointed with the food.  Portions were extremly small, in many cases one bite, served in oversiezed stone with an exaggerated amount of non edible stuff. After just a few months, we do not remember anything notable or remarkable about wht we ate. We are both professionals with knowledge of biodiversity and food history, as well as having experienced truly unique and extraordinary resturants.  We regret that Central was not such an experience.
